proof_summary: For the three exceptional exponents, the case of 9 is immediate, while modulo 27 and 81 the congruence \(10^i\equiv1+9i\) relates ordinary and weighted digit sums and forces every positive candidate with at most 3 or 9 digits to have maximal digit sum, hence to be respectively 999 or 999999999. For larger exponents, start from the 11-digit palindromic multiple \(29799999792\) of \(3^5\) and repeatedly concatenate three copies; each step adds a factor of 3 and triples the length, producing a palindromic multiple with \(11\cdot3^{n-5}<3^{n-2}\) digits and therefore a strictly smaller candidate than the corresponding all-nines number.
